What the program must do, equation by equation, with the source of every piece.
If the code and this file disagree, one of them is a bug.

## Sources, and how much to trust each

| Tag | Source | What it gives |
|---|---|---|
| **[N]** | Lux & Marchesi (1999), *Nature* 397:498 (`paper/`, local only) | The model in words, the results to reproduce (Figs 1-3). **No equations, no parameter values.** |
| **[S]** | Samanidou, Zschischang, Stauffer & **Lux** (2007), *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 70:409, sec. 9 ([arXiv physics/0701140](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0701140)) | All the equations, plus simulation details (time step, trend window, group floors). Co-written by Lux, so the most trusted. |
| **[C]** | Cristelli, Pietronero & Zaccaria (2011), sec. 4.5 ([arXiv 1101.1847](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.1847)) | The same equations; used as a cross-check. |
| **[L]** | Lux & Marchesi (2000), *IJTAF* 3:675 | The parameter tables. **Paywalled and not in hand.** Values below marked [L?] are from secondary memory and are unverified. |

## State
N traders (fixed): n_f fundamentalists, n_+ optimist chartists, n_- pessimist
chartists; n_c = n_+ + n_-. Price p, fundamental value p_f. [N][S]
Derived: opinion x = (n_+ - n_-)/n_c, chartist share z = n_c/N.

## 1. Chartists change mood (optimist <-> pessimist) [S eq 17]; [C eq 16] checks the rate form only
Rate per trader per unit time (first index = group moved TO):

    pi_{+-} = v1 (n_c/N) exp(U1)          (pessimist -> optimist)
    pi_{-+} = v1 (n_c/N) exp(-U1)         (optimist -> pessimist)
    U1 = a1 x + (a2/v1) (dp/dt)/p

a1 = herding (copy the majority mood), a2 = trend following. [N] "a weighted combination of both factors".

## 2. Traders switch strategy (chartist <-> fundamentalist) [S eqs 18-21]; [C eqs 14-15] check the rate forms only
(The formulas for U1, U21 and U22 come from [S] alone: [C] calls them "a sort of utility functions" and gives no formula.)

    pi_{+f} = v2 (n_+/N) exp(U21)   (fundamentalist -> optimist)
    pi_{f+} = v2 (n_f/N) exp(-U21)  (optimist -> fundamentalist)
    pi_{-f} = v2 (n_-/N) exp(U22)   (fundamentalist -> pessimist)
    pi_{f-} = v2 (n_f/N) exp(-U22)  (pessimist -> fundamentalist)
    U21 = a3 [ (r + (dp/dt)/v2)/p - R - s |p_f - p|/p ]
    U22 = a3 [ R - (r + (dp/dt)/v2)/p - s |p_f - p|/p ]

Each rate is proportional to the size of the group being joined: recruitment,
as in Kirman's ants. r = dividend, R = return on other investments, r/p_f = R [S].
s < 1 discounts fundamentalists' future profits [N][S].

## 3. Price [S eqs 22-25][C sec 4.5.3]

    ED_c = (n_+ - n_-) t_c
    ED_f = n_f gamma (p_f - p)/p
    up-tick rate   = max(0,  beta (ED_c + ED_f + mu)) / tick
    down-tick rate = max(0, -beta (ED_c + ED_f + mu)) / tick
    so on average  (dp/dt)/p = beta (ED_c + ED_f)        [S eq 25]

Each tick changes the price by 0.1% of the current price ([S] eq 24 text:
"Delta p = +/-0.001 p"), which is one cent at the starting price p_f = 10 [S][C].
mu is white noise [C], taken here as Gaussian with sd sigma_mu (an assumption:
[L], which would give its form, is not in hand).
**Disagreements:** [C] writes ED_f = n_f gamma (p - p_f) (wrong sign, no 1/p)
and puts mu outside beta. We follow [S]. **Units:** [S] gives the tick rate as
beta (ED + mu) (eq 24) but also says the price moves on average at
(dp/dt)/p = beta ED (eq 25). Both hold only if the tick rate is divided by the
tick size, as written above. With eq 24 taken literally, parameter set I gives a
price that hardly moves (35% of days with no change at all; tested November 2026).
We follow [S] because Lux co-wrote it, and [N] says
fundamentalists react to the *relative* deviation.

## 4. News [N][S]
ln p_f(t) - ln p_f(t-1) = eps_t, eps ~ Normal(0, sigma_eps). Gaussian, with no memory.

## 5. Simulation details [S]
- Time step dt = 0.01 of a unit of time; one unit = one trading day [N: "unit time step ... daily frequencies"].
  Probability of a switch within dt = 1 - exp(-rate*dt) (exact for a constant rate).
  ([S]'s rate*dt is the same to first order; [S] also refined dt to 0.002 in bursts.
  The exact form makes that refinement unnecessary.)
- Price ticks within dt: Poisson(rate*dt) of them. This is the exact Poisson process
  [S] approximates, so there is no cap of one tick per step.
- mu is drawn fresh each step with standard deviation sigma_mu * sqrt(0.01/dt): exactly
  [S] at dt = 0.01, and the same noise per day at any other dt.
- dp/dt = the average price change over the last 10 steps [t - 10 dt, t] [S].
  In the code, (dp/dt)/p is (p_t - p_(t-10dt)) / (0.1 p_(t-10dt)): divided by the price
  at the start of the window, not the current one (they differ by the price's move over
  the window, usually well under 1%; [S] does not say which). At the start the window
  is filled with the starting price, so the trend is 0 for the first 0.1 day.
- Order within a step: traders switch (secs. 1-2, all from the same state), then the
  price ticks (sec. 3), then the news moves the value (sec. 4) by Normal(0, sigma_eps sqrt(dt)).
- Floors: n_c and n_f never fall below a minimum, so neither group can die out for
  good (an "absorbing state") [S]. The value, 4 traders, is this project's choice:

  just enough of the moves out of that group are undone (the larger outflow first).

def shade(hex_color, amount):
    """Mix a colour with white: amount 0 = the colour, 1 = white."""
    c = np.array([int(hex_color[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5)]) / 255
    return tuple(c + (1 - c) * amount)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 1
def fig1_snapshot(paper_run, spx_run, path=FIG / "fig1_snapshot.png", days=4000):
    """The paper's Fig 1: price tracks its value, but returns are wilder than the news."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(4, 2, figsize=(13, 10), sharex=True)
    for col, (run, color, name) in enumerate([(paper_run, PAPER_MODEL, "paper-matched settings"),
                                              (spx_run, SPX_MODEL, "S&P-calibrated settings")]):
        lp, lf, z = run["lp"][:days + 1], run["lf"][:days + 1], run["z"][:days + 1]
        t = np.arange(days + 1)
        a = ax[0, col]
        a.plot(t, 100 * np.exp(lp - lp[0]), color=color, lw=1.0, label="price p")
        a.plot(t, 100 * np.exp(lf - lp[0]), ":", color=INK, lw=1.0, label="fundamental value p_f")
        a.set_title(f"a. Price and value ({name})")
        a.set_ylabel("level (start = 100)")
        a.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=True, facecolor="white", edgecolor=GRID, framealpha=0.9)
        r, eps = np.diff(lp), np.diff(lf)
        lim = 1.1 * max(np.abs(r).max(), np.abs(eps).max())
        ax[1, col].plot(t[1:], r, color=color, lw=0.4)
        ax[1, col].set_title("b. The output: daily returns ln p_t − ln p_t−1")
        ax[2, col].plot(t[1:], eps, color=NEWS, lw=0.4)
        ax[2, col].set_title("c. The input: news ε_t = ln p_f,t − ln p_f,t−1 (Gaussian)")
        for a in (ax[1, col], ax[2, col]):
            a.set_ylim(-lim, lim)
            a.set_ylabel("log change")
        ax[3, col].fill_between(t, 0, z, color=shade(color, 0.35), lw=0)
        ax[3, col].set_ylim(0, 1)
        ax[3, col].set_title("d. Share of traders who are chartists")
        ax[3, col].set_xlabel("day")
        ax[1, col].text(0.01, 0.92, f"kurtosis {stats.kurtosis(r):.1f}", transform=ax[1, col].transAxes,
                        fontsize=8.5, color=INK, va="top")
        ax[2, col].text(0.01, 0.92, f"kurtosis {stats.kurtosis(eps):.1f}",
                        transform=ax[2, col].transAxes, fontsize=8.5, color=INK, va="top")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.05, 1, 0.96))
    return plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 1. The price follows its value, but returns are far wilder than the news",
                      f"A {days:,}-day stretch of one held-out history for each setting, as in Lux & Marchesi's "
                      "Fig 1. The news (c) is a plain bell curve with no calm or wild spells; the returns (b) have "
                      "bursts of large moves, and the bursts come when many traders are chartists (d). The "
                      "S&P-calibrated model keeps few chartists most of the time, so its bursts are rarer (Fig 5).")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 2
def fig2_aggregation(paper_r, paper_news, spx_model_runs, spx, path=FIG / "fig2_tails.png",
                     paper_runs=None):
    """The paper's Fig 2: fat tails at 1 day, a cross-over to the bell curve at longer horizons."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5.2), sharey=True)
    pooled = np.concatenate(spx_model_runs)
    n_runs = len(spx_model_runs)
    panels = [(paper_r, [paper_r], PAPER_MODEL, f"a. Paper-matched model (one run, {len(paper_r):,} days)"),
              (pooled, spx_model_runs, SPX_MODEL,
               f"b. S&P-calibrated model ({n_runs} histories pooled)"),
              (spx, [spx], REAL, f"c. Real S&P 500, 1950–2026 ({len(spx):,} days)")]
    for a, (r, runs, color, title) in zip(ax, panels):
        for i, tau in enumerate(TAUS):
            x = stats.aggregate(r, tau)
            k = np.median([stats.kurtosis(stats.aggregate(h, tau)) for h in runs])
            word = "median kurtosis" if len(runs) > 1 else "kurtosis"
            plots.ccdf(a, x, f"τ = {tau:>2}: {word} {k:5.1f}", shade(color, 0.62 * i / 3))
        if r is paper_r:
            plots.ccdf(a, paper_news, "news, τ = 1", NEWS, lw=1.2, ls="-.")
        plots.gaussian_ccdf(a)
        alphas = [stats.alpha_regression(h) for h in (paper_runs if r is paper_r and paper_runs else runs)]
        note = f"tail α at τ = 1 (paper's method): {stats.alpha_regression(r) if len(runs) == 1 else np.median(alphas):.2f}"
        if r is paper_r and paper_runs:
            note += f"\n(this run; mean of {len(paper_runs)} runs: {np.mean(alphas):.2f})"
        elif len(runs) > 1:
            note += " (median of histories)"
        a.text(0.03, 0.04, note, transform=a.transAxes, fontsize=8.8, color=INK)
        a.set_xlim(0.05, 40)
        a.set_ylim(1e-5, 1.5)
        a.set_title(title)
        a.set_xlabel("|return| / standard deviation")
        a.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8)
    ax[0].set_ylabel("share of periods with a bigger move")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.07, 1, 0.94))
    return plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 2. Fat tails over one day, closer to a bell curve over 25 days",
                      "Each curve: the share of τ-day periods whose move (in standard deviations) beats x; "
                      "dashed = bell curve. Lux & Marchesi report tail α = 2.64 at τ = 1 and a cross-over to the "
                      "bell curve as τ grows. The news (dash-dot) is a bell curve at every τ. In b, kurtosis is the median "
                      "over histories (pooled, a single freak day would dominate it). Steps at small moves in a are "
                      "price ticks (0.1% each): the paper-matched model's daily sd is only about 7 ticks.")

def fig3_memory(paper_r, paper_news, spx_model_r, spx, path=FIG / "fig3_memory.png"):
    """The paper's Fig 3: DFA. Returns have no memory (H ~ 0.5); their sizes do (H ~ 0.85)."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5))
    s_long = stats.dfa_scales(len(paper_r))
    s_spx = stats.dfa_scales(len(spx))
    a = ax[0]
    plots.dfa(a, np.abs(paper_r), s_long, "|returns| (paper 0.85)", PAPER_MODEL)
    plots.dfa(a, np.abs(paper_news), s_long, "|news| (paper 0.51)", NEWS, marker="s")
    a.set_title("a. Size of moves: long memory in the output only")
    a = ax[1]
    plots.dfa(a, paper_r, s_long, "returns (paper 0.48)", PAPER_MODEL)
    plots.dfa(a, paper_news, s_long, "news (paper 0.49)", NEWS, marker="s", shift=3.0)
    a.set_title("b. Direction of moves: no memory in either")
    a = ax[2]
    plots.dfa(a, np.abs(spx), s_spx, "S&P |returns|", REAL)
    plots.dfa(a, np.abs(spx_model_r), s_spx, "model |returns|", SPX_MODEL, marker="^")
    plots.dfa(a, spx, s_spx, "S&P returns", REAL, marker="D", shift=0.2)
    plots.dfa(a, spx_model_r, s_spx, "model returns", SPX_MODEL, marker="v", shift=0.2)
    a.set_title("c. The S&P 500 and the S&P-calibrated model")
    for a in ax:
        a.set_xlabel("window n (days)")
        a.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8)
    ax[0].set_ylabel("fluctuation F(n)")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.07, 1, 0.94))
    return plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 3. Moves have no memory of direction, but a long memory of size",
                      "Detrended fluctuation analysis (Peng et al. 1994), the paper's Fig 3 method: F(n) grows like "
                      "n^H. H = 0.5 means no memory; H near 1 means calm and wild spells that last. Panels a-b: one "
                      "long paper-matched run and its news (the news curve in b is shifted up for visibility). "
                      "Panel c: one held-out history the length of the S&P (returns curves shifted down).")

def fig4_checks(no_chart, spx_runs, paper_runs, spx, path=FIG / "fig4_checks.png"):
    """The proposal's checks: no chartists -> bell curve; herding -> alpha ~ 3 like the S&P."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.8))
    a = ax[0]
    plots.ccdf(a, np.concatenate(no_chart), "no chartists", NEWS)
    plots.ccdf(a, np.concatenate(spx_runs), "with chartists (S&P settings)", SPX_MODEL)
    plots.ccdf(a, spx, "S&P 500", REAL)
    plots.gaussian_ccdf(a)
    a.set_xlim(0.05, 40)
    a.set_ylim(1e-6, 1.5)
    a.set_xlabel("|return| / standard deviation")
    a.set_ylabel("share of days with a bigger move")
    a.set_title("a. Without chartists the tails are a bell curve")
    a.legend(loc="lower left")
    groups = [("no chartists", no_chart, NEWS), ("paper-matched", paper_runs, PAPER_MODEL),
              ("S&P-calibrated", spx_runs, SPX_MODEL)]
    for a, measure, title, ref in [
            (ax[1], lambda r: stats.kurtosis(r), "b. Excess kurtosis (0 = bell curve)", 0.0),
            (ax[2], lambda r: stats.hill_alpha(r), "c. Tail exponent α (Hill, top 5%)", 3.0)]:
        ticks = []
        for i, (name, runs, color) in enumerate(groups):
            v = np.array([measure(r) for r in runs])
            jitter = np.random.default_rng(i).uniform(-0.18, 0.18, len(v))
            a.plot(i + jitter, v, "o", color=color, ms=4, alpha=0.75)
            a.plot([i - 0.28, i + 0.28], [np.median(v)] * 2, color=INK, lw=1.6)
            ticks.append(f"{name}\nmedian {np.median(v):.2f}")
        real = measure(spx)
        a.axhline(real, color=REAL, lw=1.2, label=f"S&P 500: {real:.2f}")
        a.axhline(ref, color=MUTED, ls="--", lw=1,
                  label="bell curve: 0" if ref == 0 else "inverse cubic law: α = 3")
        a.set_xticks(range(3), ticks)
        a.set_xlim(-0.5, 2.5)
        a.set_title(title)
        a.legend(loc="upper right", frameon=True, facecolor="white", edgecolor=GRID)
    ax[1].set_yscale("symlog", linthresh=1)
    ax[1].set_ylim(-0.5, None)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.07, 1, 0.94))
    return plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 4. The proposal's checks: no herding, no fat tails; with herding, α ≈ 3",
                      "Dots: held-out histories the length of the S&P 500 (40 per group; 8 long runs for "
                      "paper-matched); bars: medians. With no chartists the returns are just news, so kurtosis is "
                      "about 0 and α is large (thin tails). With chartists both fitted models have fat tails.")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 5
def fig5_mechanism(run, path=FIG / "fig5_mechanism.png", window=1500):
    """Where bursts come from: volatility rises with the chartist share."""
    r, z = run["r"], run["z"][1:]
    vol = np.abs(r) / r.std()
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(15, 6.2))
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 3, width_ratios=(1.6, 1, 1))
    peak = int(np.argmax(np.convolve(vol, np.ones(50), "same")))
    lo = max(0, min(peak - window // 2, len(r) - window))
    t = np.arange(lo, lo + window)
    a = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
    a.plot(t, r[t], color=SPX_MODEL, lw=0.5)
    a.set_title("a. The wildest stretch of one history: returns")
    a.set_ylabel("daily return")
    b = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0], sharex=a)
    b.fill_between(t, 0, z[t], color=BLUE_LIGHT, lw=0)
    b.plot(t, z[t], color=SPX_MODEL, lw=0.8)
    b.set_ylim(0, 1)
    b.set_title("…and the share of chartists at the same time")
    b.set_xlabel("day")
    edges = np.linspace(0, 1, 21)
    mid = (edges[:-1] + edges[1:]) / 2
    which = np.clip(np.digitize(z, edges) - 1, 0, 19)
    count = np.bincount(which, minlength=20)
    mean_vol = np.array([vol[which == i].mean() if count[i] >= 30 else np.nan for i in range(20)])
    c = fig.add_subplot(gs[:, 1])
    c.plot(mid, mean_vol, "o-", color=SPX_MODEL)
    c.axhline(1, color=MUTED, ls="--", lw=1)
    c.set_xlabel("share of chartists")
    c.set_ylabel("average |return| / overall sd")
    c.set_title("b. More chartists, wilder days")
    d = fig.add_subplot(gs[:, 2])
    d.bar(mid, count / count.sum(), width=0.045, color=BLUE_LIGHT, edgecolor=SPX_MODEL, lw=0.8)
    d.set_xlabel("share of chartists")
    d.set_ylabel("share of days")
    d.set_title("c. Crowded markets are rare")
    top = min(1.0, edges[np.nonzero(count)[0].max() + 1] + 0.05)
    for axis in (c, d):
        axis.set_xlim(0, top)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.07, 1, 0.94))
    return plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 5. The mechanism: bursts happen when the crowd turns to chartism",
                      "S&P-calibrated settings, one long held-out run. Lux & Marchesi: volatility is above average "
                      "when the share of noise traders nears a critical value, and the bursts end on their own when "
                      "large mispricing lures traders back to fundamentals (a: the share falls again after the burst).")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 6
def fig6_kirman(path=FIG / "fig6_kirman.png"):
    """Kirman's ants: the herding mechanism, checked against his exact solution."""
    cases = [("a. Herding: ε < (1−δ)/(N−1)", dict(N=100, eps=0.002, delta=0.01)),
             ("b. No herding: ε > (1−δ)/(N−1)", dict(N=100, eps=0.05, delta=0.01))]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 7))
    for col, (name, kw) in enumerate(cases):
        k = kirman.simulate(**kw, steps=40_000_000, seed=1)
        show = k[:5_000_000:2_000]
        ax[0, col].plot(np.arange(len(show)) * 2_000 / 1e6, show, color=BLUE, lw=0.8)
        ax[0, col].set_ylim(0, 100)
        ax[0, col].set_ylabel("ants at source A")
        ax[0, col].set_xlabel("steps (millions; first 5 of 40 shown)")
        ax[0, col].set_title(name)
        hist = np.bincount(k, minlength=101) / len(k)
        exact = kirman.stationary(**kw)
        ax[1, col].bar(np.arange(101), hist, width=0.9, color=BLUE_LIGHT, label="simulation (40M steps)")
        ax[1, col].plot(np.arange(101), exact, color=INK, lw=1.6, label="Kirman's exact answer")
        tv = 0.5 * np.abs(hist - exact).sum()
        ax[1, col].set_title(f"mismatch (total variation distance) = {tv:.3f}", fontsize=9.5)
        ax[1, col].set_xlabel("ants at source A")
        ax[1, col].set_ylabel("share of time")
        ax[1, col].legend(loc="upper center")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.06, 1, 0.94))
    return plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 6. Kirman's ants herd exactly as his math predicts",
                      "100 ants choose between two identical food sources (δ = 0.01). Rarely switching on their own "
                      "(a), they crowd at one source and then flip all at once; otherwise (b) they split about 50/50. "
                      "Bottom: time spent in each state (bars) vs the exact long-run answer (line). Lux & Marchesi "
                      "use the same recruitment rule for traders joining or leaving the chartists.")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 7
def fig7_typical(spx_runs, spx, path=FIG / "fig7_typical.png"):
    """Is the S&P 500 a typical history of the calibrated model, measure by measure?"""
    target = stats.fingerprint(spx)
    sims = [stats.fingerprint(r) for r in spx_runs]
    keys = list(stats.FINGERPRINT)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(3, 4, figsize=(15, 8.5))
    pct = {}
    for a, k in zip(ax.flat, keys):
        v = np.array([f[k] for f in sims])
        pct[k] = experiments.percentile(target[k], v)
        jitter = np.random.default_rng(0).uniform(-1, 1, len(v))
        a.plot(v, jitter, "o", color=SPX_MODEL, ms=4, alpha=0.7)
        a.axvline(target[k], color=REAL, lw=2)
        a.set_yticks([])
        a.set_ylim(-1.6, 1.6)
        if k.startswith("kurt"):
            a.set_xscale("symlog", linthresh=1)           # one freak history would squash the rest
            a.set_xlim(-0.5, 1.5 * max(v.max(), target[k]))
        unusual = pct[k] < 5 or pct[k] > 95
        a.set_title(f"{LABEL[k]}: S&P at {pct[k]:.0f}%" + ("  ← unusual" if unusual else ""),
                    fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
        a.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    ax.flat[-1].axis("off")
    ok = sum(5 <= p <= 95 for p in pct.values())
    ax.flat[-1].text(0, 0.5, f"{ok} of {len(keys)} measures:\nthe S&P sits inside the\nmiddle 90% of model\nhistories",
                     fontsize=12, color=INK, va="center")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.06, 1, 0.94))
    plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 7. Does the real S&P 500 look like one more history of the model?",
               f"Dots: {len(sims)} held-out histories of the S&P-calibrated model, each {len(spx):,} days like the "
               "S&P 500 sample; black line: the S&P 500. The percentage is the share of histories below the S&P; "
               "below 5% or above 95% marks a measure where the S&P is unusual for the model. Kurtosis axes are "
               "logarithmic above 1, because one history has a freak event (kurtosis in the thousands).")
    return pct


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 8
def fig8_out_of_sample(pool, p, path=FIG / "fig8_out_of_sample.png", n=20):
    """Markets the calibration never saw: percentile of each among model histories."""
    keys = [k for k in stats.FINGERPRINT if k != "sd"]     # shape only: volatility differs by asset
    if not 1 <= n <= len(HELD_OUT) // 2:
        raise ValueError(f"n must be between 1 and {len(HELD_OUT) // 2}, got {n}")
    # (name, returns, seeds): the indexes use held-out seeds 1000-1019, the stocks
    # their own, 1020-1039, so the stocks are not compared with shorter copies of
    # the very histories the indexes were compared with.
    series = [("S&P 500 1928–", market_data.returns("spx_1928").values, HELD_OUT[:n]),
              ("Nasdaq-100 1985–", market_data.returns("ndx").values, HELD_OUT[:n])]
    series += [(t, market_data.stock_returns(t).values, HELD_OUT[n:2 * n])
               for t in market_data.stock_tickers()]
    cache, rows = {}, []
    for name, r, seeds in series:
        if (len(r), seeds) not in cache:
            cache[len(r), seeds] = [stats.fingerprint(x)
                                    for x in experiments.returns(p, seeds, len(r), pool=pool)]
        f = stats.fingerprint(r)
        rows.append([experiments.percentile(f[k], [s[k] for s in cache[len(r), seeds]]) for k in keys])
    rows = np.array(rows)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 9))
    cmap = matplotlib_diverging()
    im = ax.imshow(rows, cmap=cmap, vmin=0, vmax=100, aspect="auto")
    for i in range(rows.shape[0]):
        for j in range(rows.shape[1]):
            v = rows[i, j]
            ax.text(j, i, f"{v:.0f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7.5,
                    color="white" if v < 10 or v > 90 else INK)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(keys)), [LABEL[k] for k in keys], rotation=30, ha="right")
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(series)), [s[0] for s in series], fontsize=8.5)
    ax.grid(False)
    ax.axhline(1.5, color="white", lw=3)
    cb = fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.03)
    cb.set_label("percentile among model histories (50 = typical)")
    unusual = int(np.sum((rows < 5) | (rows > 95)))
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.06, 1, 0.95))
    plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 8. Markets the model never saw: two indexes and 20 stocks",
               f"Each cell: where a real market sits among {n} S&P-calibrated histories of the same length (0-100). "
               f"Middle colours = typical; dark ends = unusual (below 5 or above 95): {unusual} of {rows.size} cells. "
               "Volatility (sd) is left out: stocks move more than the index by nature. Stocks are price-only "
               "(no dividends) and are today's large companies (survivorship bias).")
    return rows, keys, [s[0] for s in series]


def matplotlib_diverging():
    from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap
    return LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("pct", [BLUE, "#f2f1ec", ORANGE])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 9
def _robust(args):
    i, days = args
    p = calibrate.draw(np.random.default_rng(50_000 + i), calibrate.RANGES)
    try:
        r = model.simulate(p, days + calibrate.BURN, seed=7)["r"][calibrate.BURN:]
    except model.RunawayError:
        return None
    return stats.kurtosis(r), stats.alpha_regression(r), stats.hurst(np.abs(r), stats.dfa_scales(days))


def _robust_base(args):
    """The no-chartist yardstick for Fig 9: kurtosis and H of |returns|."""
    i, days = args
    p = calibrate.draw(np.random.default_rng(60_000 + i), calibrate.RANGES)
    r = model.simulate(p, days, seed=7, chartists=False)["r"]
    return stats.kurtosis(r), stats.hurst(np.abs(r), stats.dfa_scales(days))


def fig9_robustness(pool, n=400, days=20_000, path=FIG / "fig9_robustness.png"):
    """The paper: results hold 'for an open set of parameter values'. Do they?"""
    # chunksize=1: run times differ a lot (runaways stop early), so hand out one at a time
    out = pool.map(_robust, [(i, days) for i in range(n)], chunksize=1)
    ok = np.array([o for o in out if o is not None])
    base = np.array(pool.map(_robust_base, [(i, days) for i in range(40)], chunksize=1))
    base_k, base_h = base[:, 0], base[:, 1]
    fat = ok[:, 0] > base_k.max()
    memory = ok[:, 2] > base_h.max()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5.2))
    a = ax[0]
    a.scatter(ok[~memory, 1], ok[~memory, 2], s=12, color=ORANGE_LIGHT, label="no volatility memory")
    a.scatter(ok[memory, 1], ok[memory, 2], s=12, color=PAPER_MODEL, label="volatility memory")
    a.plot(2.64, 0.85, "*", ms=16, color=INK, label="Lux & Marchesi (1999)")
    a.axhline(base_h.max(), color=NEWS, ls="--", lw=1.2, label="largest value with no chartists")
    a.set_xlabel("tail α (paper's method)")
    a.set_ylabel("H of |returns|")
    a.set_xlim(1, 4.5)
    a.set_title("a. Every setting that did not run away")
    a.legend(loc="upper right", frameon=True, facecolor="white", edgecolor=GRID)
    b = ax[1]
    counts = [n - len(ok), int(np.sum(~fat)), int(np.sum(fat & ~memory)), int(np.sum(fat & memory))]
    names = ["ran away\n(endless bubble)", "thin tails", "fat tails,\nno memory", "fat tails\nand memory"]
    colors = [MUTED, NEWS, ORANGE_LIGHT, PAPER_MODEL]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 10
MIN_SURVIVORS = 5     # Fig 10: a median of fewer surviving histories is not shown


def _dial(pool, p, a1s, days, n):
    """For each a1: (share of histories that did not run away, then the median
    kurtosis, Hill alpha and worst day in sd over the survivors). The medians are
    NaN (not drawn) when fewer than min(MIN_SURVIVORS, n) histories survived."""
    rows = []
    for a1 in a1s:
        out = experiments.histories(dict(p, a1=float(a1)), HELD_OUT[:n], days, pool=pool)
        ok = [h["r"] for h in out if h is not None]
        enough = len(ok) >= min(MIN_SURVIVORS, n)
        rows.append((len(ok) / n,
                     np.median([stats.kurtosis(r) for r in ok]) if enough else np.nan,
                     np.median([stats.hill_alpha(r) for r in ok]) if enough else np.nan,
                     np.median([np.abs(r).max() / r.std() for r in ok]) if enough else np.nan))
    return np.array(rows)

             "paper-matched": (_dial(pool, paper_p, a1s, days, n), paper_p, PAPER_MODEL, "s")}
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(16, 4.6))
    titles = ["a. Histories without a runaway", "b. Excess kurtosis (median)",

    for name, (rows, p, color, marker) in dials.items():
        for j, a in enumerate(ax):

               f"endless bubble. Missing points in b-d: fewer than {MIN_SURVIVORS} histories survived, too few for a median. "

417	MIN_SURVIVORS = 5     # Fig 10: a median of fewer surviving histories is not shown

420	def _dial(pool, p, a1s, days, n):
421	    """For each a1: (share of histories that did not run away, then the median
422	    kurtosis, Hill alpha and worst day in sd over the survivors). The medians are
423	    NaN (not drawn) when fewer than min(MIN_SURVIVORS, n) histories survived."""
424	    rows = []
425	    for a1 in a1s:
426	        out = experiments.histories(dict(p, a1=float(a1)), HELD_OUT[:n], days, pool=pool)
427	        ok = [h["r"] for h in out if h is not None]
428	        enough = len(ok) >= min(MIN_SURVIVORS, n)
429	        rows.append((len(ok) / n,
430	                     np.median([stats.kurtosis(r) for r in ok]) if enough else np.nan,
431	                     np.median([stats.hill_alpha(r) for r in ok]) if enough else np.nan,
432	                     np.median([np.abs(r).max() / r.std() for r in ok]) if enough else np.nan))
433	    return np.array(rows)

"""Make every results figure (figures/fig1-11*.png), explained in figures/RESULTS.md.

Run:  python3 make_figures.py        (a few minutes with numba, using every core)

Two fitted settings are used (both from python3 -m herding.calibrate):
    paper-matched  settings/paper.json  reproduces Lux & Marchesi (1999)'s numbers
    S&P-calibrated settings/spx.json    reproduces the S&P 500's fingerprint
Every model check uses held-out seeds that neither fit ever saw.
"""
from multiprocessing import Pool

import numpy as np

from herding import calibrate, experiments, kirman, market_data, model, plots, policy, stats
from herding.plots import (BLUE, BLUE_LIGHT, GRID, INK, MUTED, NEWS, ORANGE,
                           ORANGE_LIGHT, PAPER_MODEL, REAL, SECOND, SPX_MODEL, plt)

FIG = market_data.ROOT / "figures"
HELD_OUT = calibrate.HELD_OUT_SEEDS            # 40 seeds, never used for fitting
LONG = 100_000                                 # days in a long run (the paper's Figs 2-3)
BREAKER_SEEDS = tuple(range(3000, 3200))       # policy experiments: their own seeds
SURPRISE_SEEDS = tuple(range(4000, 4400))
TAUS = (1, 5, 15, 25)                          # the paper's aggregation horizons
LABEL = {k: k for k in stats.FINGERPRINT}
LABEL.update(sd="daily sd", kurtosis="kurtosis", alpha_hill="tail α (Hill)",
             alpha_reg="tail α (paper's fit)", ac_r_1="next-day corr.",
             ac_abs_1="clustering, 1 day", ac_abs_50="clustering, 50 days",
             H="H of returns", H_abs="H of |returns|", kurt_5="kurtosis, 5 days",
             kurt_25="kurtosis, 25 days")


def shade(hex_color, amount):
    """Mix a colour with white: amount 0 = the colour, 1 = white."""
    c = np.array([int(hex_color[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5)]) / 255
    return tuple(c + (1 - c) * amount)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 1
def fig1_snapshot(paper_run, spx_run, path=FIG / "fig1_snapshot.png", days=4000):
    """The paper's Fig 1: price tracks its value, but returns are wilder than the news."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(4, 2, figsize=(13, 10), sharex=True)
    for col, (run, color, name) in enumerate([(paper_run, PAPER_MODEL, "paper-matched settings"),
                                              (spx_run, SPX_MODEL, "S&P-calibrated settings")]):
        lp, lf, z = run["lp"][:days + 1], run["lf"][:days + 1], run["z"][:days + 1]
        t = np.arange(days + 1)
        a = ax[0, col]
        a.plot(t, 100 * np.exp(lp - lp[0]), color=color, lw=1.0, label="price p")
        a.plot(t, 100 * np.exp(lf - lp[0]), ":", color=INK, lw=1.0, label="fundamental value p_f")
        a.set_title(f"a. Price and value ({name})")
        a.set_ylabel("level (start = 100)")
        a.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=True, facecolor="white", edgecolor=GRID, framealpha=0.9)
        r, eps = np.diff(lp), np.diff(lf)
        lim = 1.1 * max(np.abs(r).max(), np.abs(eps).max())
        ax[1, col].plot(t[1:], r, color=color, lw=0.4)
        ax[1, col].set_title("b. The output: daily returns ln p_t − ln p_t−1")
        ax[2, col].plot(t[1:], eps, color=NEWS, lw=0.4)
        ax[2, col].set_title("c. The input: news ε_t = ln p_f,t − ln p_f,t−1 (Gaussian)")
        for a in (ax[1, col], ax[2, col]):
            a.set_ylim(-lim, lim)
            a.set_ylabel("log change")
        ax[3, col].fill_between(t, 0, z, color=shade(color, 0.35), lw=0)
        ax[3, col].set_ylim(0, 1)
        ax[3, col].set_title("d. Share of traders who are chartists")
        ax[3, col].set_xlabel("day")
        ax[1, col].text(0.01, 0.92, f"kurtosis {stats.kurtosis(r):.1f}", transform=ax[1, col].transAxes,
                        fontsize=8.5, color=INK, va="top")
        ax[2, col].text(0.01, 0.92, f"kurtosis {stats.kurtosis(eps):.1f}",
                        transform=ax[2, col].transAxes, fontsize=8.5, color=INK, va="top")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.05, 1, 0.96))
    return plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 1. The price follows its value, but returns are far wilder than the news",
                      f"A {days:,}-day stretch of one held-out history for each setting, as in Lux & Marchesi's "
                      "Fig 1. The news (c) is a plain bell curve with no calm or wild spells; the returns (b) have "
                      "bursts of large moves, and the bursts come when many traders are chartists (d). The "
                      "S&P-calibrated model keeps few chartists most of the time, so its bursts are rarer (Fig 5).")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 2
def fig2_aggregation(paper_r, paper_news, spx_model_runs, spx, path=FIG / "fig2_tails.png",
                     paper_runs=None):
    """The paper's Fig 2: fat tails at 1 day, a cross-over to the bell curve at longer horizons."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5.2), sharey=True)
    pooled = np.concatenate(spx_model_runs)
    n_runs = len(spx_model_runs)
    panels = [(paper_r, [paper_r], PAPER_MODEL, f"a. Paper-matched model (one run, {len(paper_r):,} days)"),
              (pooled, spx_model_runs, SPX_MODEL,
               f"b. S&P-calibrated model ({n_runs} histories pooled)"),
              (spx, [spx], REAL, f"c. Real S&P 500, 1950–2026 ({len(spx):,} days)")]
    for a, (r, runs, color, title) in zip(ax, panels):
        for i, tau in enumerate(TAUS):
            x = stats.aggregate(r, tau)
            k = np.median([stats.kurtosis(stats.aggregate(h, tau)) for h in runs])
            word = "median kurtosis" if len(runs) > 1 else "kurtosis"
            plots.ccdf(a, x, f"τ = {tau:>2}: {word} {k:5.1f}", shade(color, 0.62 * i / 3))
        if r is paper_r:
            plots.ccdf(a, paper_news, "news, τ = 1", NEWS, lw=1.2, ls="-.")
        plots.gaussian_ccdf(a)
        alphas = [stats.alpha_regression(h) for h in (paper_runs if r is paper_r and paper_runs else runs)]
        note = f"tail α at τ = 1 (paper's method): {stats.alpha_regression(r) if len(runs) == 1 else np.median(alphas):.2f}"
        if r is paper_r and paper_runs:
            note += f"\n(this run; mean of {len(paper_runs)} runs: {np.mean(alphas):.2f})"
        elif len(runs) > 1:
            note += " (median of histories)"
        a.text(0.03, 0.04, note, transform=a.transAxes, fontsize=8.8, color=INK)
        a.set_xlim(0.05, 40)
        a.set_ylim(1e-5, 1.5)
        a.set_title(title)
        a.set_xlabel("|return| / standard deviation")
        a.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8)
    ax[0].set_ylabel("share of periods with a bigger move")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.07, 1, 0.94))
    return plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 2. Fat tails over one day, closer to a bell curve over 25 days",
                      "Each curve: the share of τ-day periods whose move (in standard deviations) beats x; "
                      "dashed = bell curve. Lux & Marchesi report tail α = 2.64 at τ = 1 and a cross-over to the "
                      "bell curve as τ grows. The news (dash-dot) is a bell curve at every τ. In b, kurtosis is the median "
                      "over histories (pooled, a single freak day would dominate it). Steps at small moves in a are "
                      "price ticks (0.1% each): the paper-matched model's daily sd is only about 7 ticks.")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 3
def fig3_memory(paper_r, paper_news, spx_model_r, spx, path=FIG / "fig3_memory.png"):
    """The paper's Fig 3: DFA. Returns have no memory (H ~ 0.5); their sizes do (H ~ 0.85)."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5))
    s_long = stats.dfa_scales(len(paper_r))
    s_spx = stats.dfa_scales(len(spx))
    a = ax[0]
    plots.dfa(a, np.abs(paper_r), s_long, "|returns| (paper 0.85)", PAPER_MODEL)
    plots.dfa(a, np.abs(paper_news), s_long, "|news| (paper 0.51)", NEWS, marker="s")
    a.set_title("a. Size of moves: long memory in the output only")
    a = ax[1]
    plots.dfa(a, paper_r, s_long, "returns (paper 0.48)", PAPER_MODEL)
    plots.dfa(a, paper_news, s_long, "news (paper 0.49)", NEWS, marker="s", shift=3.0)
    a.set_title("b. Direction of moves: no memory in either")
    a = ax[2]
    plots.dfa(a, np.abs(spx), s_spx, "S&P |returns|", REAL)
    plots.dfa(a, np.abs(spx_model_r), s_spx, "model |returns|", SPX_MODEL, marker="^")
    plots.dfa(a, spx, s_spx, "S&P returns", REAL, marker="D", shift=0.2)
    plots.dfa(a, spx_model_r, s_spx, "model returns", SPX_MODEL, marker="v", shift=0.2)
    a.set_title("c. The S&P 500 and the S&P-calibrated model")
    for a in ax:
        a.set_xlabel("window n (days)")
        a.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8)
    ax[0].set_ylabel("fluctuation F(n)")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.07, 1, 0.94))
    return plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 3. Moves have no memory of direction, but a long memory of size",
                      "Detrended fluctuation analysis (Peng et al. 1994), the paper's Fig 3 method: F(n) grows like "
                      "n^H. H = 0.5 means no memory; H near 1 means calm and wild spells that last. Panels a-b: one "
                      "long paper-matched run and its news (the news curve in b is shifted up for visibility). "
                      "Panel c: one held-out history the length of the S&P (returns curves shifted down).")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 4
def fig4_checks(no_chart, spx_runs, paper_runs, spx, path=FIG / "fig4_checks.png"):
    """The proposal's checks: no chartists -> bell curve; herding -> alpha ~ 3 like the S&P."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.8))
    a = ax[0]
    plots.ccdf(a, np.concatenate(no_chart), "no chartists", NEWS)
    plots.ccdf(a, np.concatenate(spx_runs), "with chartists (S&P settings)", SPX_MODEL)
    plots.ccdf(a, spx, "S&P 500", REAL)
    plots.gaussian_ccdf(a)
    a.set_xlim(0.05, 40)
    a.set_ylim(1e-6, 1.5)
    a.set_xlabel("|return| / standard deviation")
    a.set_ylabel("share of days with a bigger move")
    a.set_title("a. Without chartists the tails are a bell curve")
    a.legend(loc="lower left")
    groups = [("no chartists", no_chart, NEWS), ("paper-matched", paper_runs, PAPER_MODEL),
              ("S&P-calibrated", spx_runs, SPX_MODEL)]
    for a, measure, title, ref in [
            (ax[1], lambda r: stats.kurtosis(r), "b. Excess kurtosis (0 = bell curve)", 0.0),
            (ax[2], lambda r: stats.hill_alpha(r), "c. Tail exponent α (Hill, top 5%)", 3.0)]:
        ticks = []
        for i, (name, runs, color) in enumerate(groups):
            v = np.array([measure(r) for r in runs])
            jitter = np.random.default_rng(i).uniform(-0.18, 0.18, len(v))
            a.plot(i + jitter, v, "o", color=color, ms=4, alpha=0.75)
            a.plot([i - 0.28, i + 0.28], [np.median(v)] * 2, color=INK, lw=1.6)
            ticks.append(f"{name}\nmedian {np.median(v):.2f}")
        real = measure(spx)
        a.axhline(real, color=REAL, lw=1.2, label=f"S&P 500: {real:.2f}")
        a.axhline(ref, color=MUTED, ls="--", lw=1,
                  label="bell curve: 0" if ref == 0 else "inverse cubic law: α = 3")
        a.set_xticks(range(3), ticks)
        a.set_xlim(-0.5, 2.5)
        a.set_title(title)
        a.legend(loc="upper right", frameon=True, facecolor="white", edgecolor=GRID)
    ax[1].set_yscale("symlog", linthresh=1)
    ax[1].set_ylim(-0.5, None)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.07, 1, 0.94))
    return plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 4. The proposal's checks: no herding, no fat tails; with herding, α ≈ 3",
                      "Dots: held-out histories the length of the S&P 500 (40 per group; 8 long runs for "
                      "paper-matched); bars: medians. With no chartists the returns are just news, so kurtosis is "
                      "about 0 and α is large (thin tails). With chartists both fitted models have fat tails.")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 5
def fig5_mechanism(run, path=FIG / "fig5_mechanism.png", window=1500):
    """Where bursts come from: volatility rises with the chartist share."""
    r, z = run["r"], run["z"][1:]
    vol = np.abs(r) / r.std()
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(15, 6.2))
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 3, width_ratios=(1.6, 1, 1))
    peak = int(np.argmax(np.convolve(vol, np.ones(50), "same")))
    lo = max(0, min(peak - window // 2, len(r) - window))
    t = np.arange(lo, lo + window)
    a = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
    a.plot(t, r[t], color=SPX_MODEL, lw=0.5)
    a.set_title("a. The wildest stretch of one history: returns")
    a.set_ylabel("daily return")
    b = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0], sharex=a)
    b.fill_between(t, 0, z[t], color=BLUE_LIGHT, lw=0)
    b.plot(t, z[t], color=SPX_MODEL, lw=0.8)
    b.set_ylim(0, 1)
    b.set_title("…and the share of chartists at the same time")
    b.set_xlabel("day")
    edges = np.linspace(0, 1, 21)
    mid = (edges[:-1] + edges[1:]) / 2
    which = np.clip(np.digitize(z, edges) - 1, 0, 19)
    count = np.bincount(which, minlength=20)
    mean_vol = np.array([vol[which == i].mean() if count[i] >= 30 else np.nan for i in range(20)])
    c = fig.add_subplot(gs[:, 1])
    c.plot(mid, mean_vol, "o-", color=SPX_MODEL)
    c.axhline(1, color=MUTED, ls="--", lw=1)
    c.set_xlabel("share of chartists")
    c.set_ylabel("average |return| / overall sd")
    c.set_title("b. More chartists, wilder days")
    d = fig.add_subplot(gs[:, 2])
    d.bar(mid, count / count.sum(), width=0.045, color=BLUE_LIGHT, edgecolor=SPX_MODEL, lw=0.8)
    d.set_xlabel("share of chartists")
    d.set_ylabel("share of days")
    d.set_title("c. Crowded markets are rare")
    top = min(1.0, edges[np.nonzero(count)[0].max() + 1] + 0.05)
    for axis in (c, d):
        axis.set_xlim(0, top)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.07, 1, 0.94))
    return plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 5. The mechanism: bursts happen when the crowd turns to chartism",
                      "S&P-calibrated settings, one long held-out run. Lux & Marchesi: volatility is above average "
                      "when the share of noise traders nears a critical value, and the bursts end on their own when "
                      "large mispricing lures traders back to fundamentals (a: the share falls again after the burst).")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 6
def fig6_kirman(path=FIG / "fig6_kirman.png"):
    """Kirman's ants: the herding mechanism, checked against his exact solution."""
    cases = [("a. Herding: ε < (1−δ)/(N−1)", dict(N=100, eps=0.002, delta=0.01)),
             ("b. No herding: ε > (1−δ)/(N−1)", dict(N=100, eps=0.05, delta=0.01))]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 7))
    for col, (name, kw) in enumerate(cases):
        k = kirman.simulate(**kw, steps=40_000_000, seed=1)
        show = k[:5_000_000:2_000]
        ax[0, col].plot(np.arange(len(show)) * 2_000 / 1e6, show, color=BLUE, lw=0.8)
        ax[0, col].set_ylim(0, 100)
        ax[0, col].set_ylabel("ants at source A")
        ax[0, col].set_xlabel("steps (millions; first 5 of 40 shown)")
        ax[0, col].set_title(name)
        hist = np.bincount(k, minlength=101) / len(k)
        exact = kirman.stationary(**kw)
        ax[1, col].bar(np.arange(101), hist, width=0.9, color=BLUE_LIGHT, label="simulation (40M steps)")
        ax[1, col].plot(np.arange(101), exact, color=INK, lw=1.6, label="Kirman's exact answer")
        tv = 0.5 * np.abs(hist - exact).sum()
        ax[1, col].set_title(f"mismatch (total variation distance) = {tv:.3f}", fontsize=9.5)
        ax[1, col].set_xlabel("ants at source A")
        ax[1, col].set_ylabel("share of time")
        ax[1, col].legend(loc="upper center")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.06, 1, 0.94))
    return plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 6. Kirman's ants herd exactly as his math predicts",
                      "100 ants choose between two identical food sources (δ = 0.01). Rarely switching on their own "
                      "(a), they crowd at one source and then flip all at once; otherwise (b) they split about 50/50. "
                      "Bottom: time spent in each state (bars) vs the exact long-run answer (line). Lux & Marchesi "
                      "use the same recruitment rule for traders joining or leaving the chartists.")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 7
def fig7_typical(spx_runs, spx, path=FIG / "fig7_typical.png"):
    """Is the S&P 500 a typical history of the calibrated model, measure by measure?"""
    target = stats.fingerprint(spx)
    sims = [stats.fingerprint(r) for r in spx_runs]
    keys = list(stats.FINGERPRINT)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(3, 4, figsize=(15, 8.5))
    pct = {}
    for a, k in zip(ax.flat, keys):
        v = np.array([f[k] for f in sims])
        pct[k] = experiments.percentile(target[k], v)
        jitter = np.random.default_rng(0).uniform(-1, 1, len(v))
        a.plot(v, jitter, "o", color=SPX_MODEL, ms=4, alpha=0.7)
        a.axvline(target[k], color=REAL, lw=2)
        a.set_yticks([])
        a.set_ylim(-1.6, 1.6)
        if k.startswith("kurt"):
            a.set_xscale("symlog", linthresh=1)           # one freak history would squash the rest
            a.set_xlim(-0.5, 1.5 * max(v.max(), target[k]))
        unusual = pct[k] < 5 or pct[k] > 95
        a.set_title(f"{LABEL[k]}: S&P at {pct[k]:.0f}%" + ("  ← unusual" if unusual else ""),
                    fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
        a.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    ax.flat[-1].axis("off")
    ok = sum(5 <= p <= 95 for p in pct.values())
    ax.flat[-1].text(0, 0.5, f"{ok} of {len(keys)} measures:\nthe S&P sits inside the\nmiddle 90% of model\nhistories",
                     fontsize=12, color=INK, va="center")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.06, 1, 0.94))
    plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 7. Does the real S&P 500 look like one more history of the model?",
               f"Dots: {len(sims)} held-out histories of the S&P-calibrated model, each {len(spx):,} days like the "
               "S&P 500 sample; black line: the S&P 500. The percentage is the share of histories below the S&P; "
               "below 5% or above 95% marks a measure where the S&P is unusual for the model. Kurtosis axes are "
               "logarithmic above 1, because one history has a freak event (kurtosis in the thousands).")
    return pct


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 8
def fig8_out_of_sample(pool, p, path=FIG / "fig8_out_of_sample.png", n=20):
    """Markets the calibration never saw: percentile of each among model histories."""
    keys = [k for k in stats.FINGERPRINT if k != "sd"]     # shape only: volatility differs by asset
    if not 1 <= n <= len(HELD_OUT) // 2:
        raise ValueError(f"n must be between 1 and {len(HELD_OUT) // 2}, got {n}")
    # (name, returns, seeds): the indexes use held-out seeds 1000-1019, the stocks
    # their own, 1020-1039, so the stocks are not compared with shorter copies of
    # the very histories the indexes were compared with.
    series = [("S&P 500 1928–", market_data.returns("spx_1928").values, HELD_OUT[:n]),
              ("Nasdaq-100 1985–", market_data.returns("ndx").values, HELD_OUT[:n])]
    series += [(t, market_data.stock_returns(t).values, HELD_OUT[n:2 * n])
               for t in market_data.stock_tickers()]
    cache, rows = {}, []
    for name, r, seeds in series:
        if (len(r), seeds) not in cache:
            cache[len(r), seeds] = [stats.fingerprint(x)
                                    for x in experiments.returns(p, seeds, len(r), pool=pool)]
        f = stats.fingerprint(r)
        rows.append([experiments.percentile(f[k], [s[k] for s in cache[len(r), seeds]]) for k in keys])
    rows = np.array(rows)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 9))
    cmap = matplotlib_diverging()
    im = ax.imshow(rows, cmap=cmap, vmin=0, vmax=100, aspect="auto")
    for i in range(rows.shape[0]):
        for j in range(rows.shape[1]):
            v = rows[i, j]
            ax.text(j, i, f"{v:.0f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7.5,
                    color="white" if v < 10 or v > 90 else INK)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(keys)), [LABEL[k] for k in keys], rotation=30, ha="right")
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(series)), [s[0] for s in series], fontsize=8.5)
    ax.grid(False)
    ax.axhline(1.5, color="white", lw=3)
    cb = fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.03)
    cb.set_label("percentile among model histories (50 = typical)")
    unusual = int(np.sum((rows < 5) | (rows > 95)))
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.06, 1, 0.95))
    plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 8. Markets the model never saw: two indexes and 20 stocks",
               f"Each cell: where a real market sits among {n} S&P-calibrated histories of the same length (0-100). "
               f"Middle colours = typical; dark ends = unusual (below 5 or above 95): {unusual} of {rows.size} cells. "
               "Volatility (sd) is left out: stocks move more than the index by nature. Stocks are price-only "
               "(no dividends) and are today's large companies (survivorship bias).")
    return rows, keys, [s[0] for s in series]


def matplotlib_diverging():
    from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap
    return LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("pct", [BLUE, "#f2f1ec", ORANGE])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 9
def _robust(args):
    i, days = args
    p = calibrate.draw(np.random.default_rng(50_000 + i), calibrate.RANGES)
    try:
        r = model.simulate(p, days + calibrate.BURN, seed=7)["r"][calibrate.BURN:]
    except model.RunawayError:
        return None
    return stats.kurtosis(r), stats.alpha_regression(r), stats.hurst(np.abs(r), stats.dfa_scales(days))


def _robust_base(args):
    """The no-chartist yardstick for Fig 9: kurtosis and H of |returns|."""
    i, days = args
    p = calibrate.draw(np.random.default_rng(60_000 + i), calibrate.RANGES)
    r = model.simulate(p, days, seed=7, chartists=False)["r"]
    return stats.kurtosis(r), stats.hurst(np.abs(r), stats.dfa_scales(days))


def fig9_robustness(pool, n=400, days=20_000, path=FIG / "fig9_robustness.png"):
    """The paper: results hold 'for an open set of parameter values'. Do they?"""
    # chunksize=1: run times differ a lot (runaways stop early), so hand out one at a time
    out = pool.map(_robust, [(i, days) for i in range(n)], chunksize=1)
    ok = np.array([o for o in out if o is not None])
    base = np.array(pool.map(_robust_base, [(i, days) for i in range(40)], chunksize=1))
    base_k, base_h = base[:, 0], base[:, 1]
    fat = ok[:, 0] > base_k.max()
    memory = ok[:, 2] > base_h.max()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5.2))
    a = ax[0]
    a.scatter(ok[~memory, 1], ok[~memory, 2], s=12, color=ORANGE_LIGHT, label="no volatility memory")
    a.scatter(ok[memory, 1], ok[memory, 2], s=12, color=PAPER_MODEL, label="volatility memory")
    a.plot(2.64, 0.85, "*", ms=16, color=INK, label="Lux & Marchesi (1999)")
    a.axhline(base_h.max(), color=NEWS, ls="--", lw=1.2, label="largest value with no chartists")
    a.set_xlabel("tail α (paper's method)")
    a.set_ylabel("H of |returns|")
    a.set_xlim(1, 4.5)
    a.set_title("a. Every setting that did not run away")
    a.legend(loc="upper right", frameon=True, facecolor="white", edgecolor=GRID)
    b = ax[1]
    counts = [n - len(ok), int(np.sum(~fat)), int(np.sum(fat & ~memory)), int(np.sum(fat & memory))]
    names = ["ran away\n(endless bubble)", "thin tails", "fat tails,\nno memory", "fat tails\nand memory"]
    colors = [MUTED, NEWS, ORANGE_LIGHT, PAPER_MODEL]
    b.bar(range(4), np.array(counts) / n * 100, color=colors, width=0.6)
    for i, c in enumerate(counts):
        b.text(i, c / n * 100, f"{c / n:.0%}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
    b.set_xticks(range(4), names)
    b.set_ylabel(f"share of {n} random settings (%)")
    b.set_title("b. What random settings produce")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.07, 1, 0.94))
    plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 9. Most stable settings give fat tails and memory, but many settings are unstable",
               f"{n} settings drawn at random from the fitting ranges, one {days:,}-day run each. 'Fat tails' = "
               "kurtosis above every no-chartist run; 'memory' = H of |returns| above every no-chartist run "
               "(dashed line). Many random settings end in an endless bubble, so the paper's 'open set' of good "
               "parameters is real but far from all of them.")
    return dict(n=n, runaway=counts[0], thin=counts[1], fat_only=counts[2], fat_memory=counts[3])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 10
MIN_SURVIVORS = 5     # Fig 10: a median of fewer surviving histories is not shown


def _dial(pool, p, a1s, days, n):
    """For each a1: (share of histories that did not run away, then the median
    kurtosis, Hill alpha and worst day in sd over the survivors). The medians are
    NaN (not drawn) when fewer than min(MIN_SURVIVORS, n) histories survived."""
    rows = []
    for a1 in a1s:
        out = experiments.histories(dict(p, a1=float(a1)), HELD_OUT[:n], days, pool=pool)
        ok = [h["r"] for h in out if h is not None]
        enough = len(ok) >= min(MIN_SURVIVORS, n)
        rows.append((len(ok) / n,
                     np.median([stats.kurtosis(r) for r in ok]) if enough else np.nan,
                     np.median([stats.hill_alpha(r) for r in ok]) if enough else np.nan,
                     np.median([np.abs(r).max() / r.std() for r in ok]) if enough else np.nan))
    return np.array(rows)


def fig10_herding(pool, spx_p, paper_p, days, path=FIG / "fig10_herding.png", n=12):
    """The project question as a dial: what does stronger mood herding (a1) do?"""
    a1s = np.round(np.linspace(0, 1.4, 8), 2)
    dials = {"S&P-calibrated": (_dial(pool, spx_p, a1s, days, n), spx_p, SPX_MODEL, "o"),
             "paper-matched": (_dial(pool, paper_p, a1s, days, n), paper_p, PAPER_MODEL, "s")}
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(16, 4.6))
    titles = ["a. Histories without a runaway", "b. Excess kurtosis (median)",
              "c. Tail α, Hill (median)", "d. Worst day, in sd (median)"]
    for name, (rows, p, color, marker) in dials.items():
        for j, a in enumerate(ax):
            a.plot(a1s, rows[:, j], marker + "-", color=color, label=name)
            a.axvline(p["a1"], color=color, ls=":", lw=1.2)
    for j, a in enumerate(ax):
        a.set_xlabel("herding strength a1")
        a.set_title(titles[j])
    ax[0].set_ylim(-0.05, 1.05)
    ax[0].legend(loc="lower right")
    ax[2].axhline(3, color=MUTED, ls="--", lw=1)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.09, 1, 0.93))
    plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 10. Turning the herding dial",
               f"Each fitted setting with only a1 (how strongly chartists copy the majority mood) changed; dotted "
               f"lines mark the fitted a1. {n} held-out histories of {days:,} days at each value; a runaway is an "
               f"endless bubble. Missing points in b-d: fewer than {MIN_SURVIVORS} histories survived, too few for a median. "
               "This is the dial the web app will expose.")
    return a1s, {k: v[0] for k, v in dials.items()}

def fig11_policy(pool, p, spx, path=FIG / "fig11_policy.png", breaker_seeds=BREAKER_SEEDS,
                 surprise_seeds=SURPRISE_SEEDS):
    """Extension: circuit breakers and a policy surprise, in S&P-calibrated markets."""
    days = len(spx)

    rules, scale = policy.scaled_breakers(sd, np.std(spx))

    surprise, bad_s = policy.surprise_experiment(pool, p, surprise_seeds)
    # (fewer than 2 histories with a pause, e.g. in a short test run: nothing to compare)

             if len(events["on"][k]) >= 2 else (np.nan, np.nan, np.nan) for k in policy.EVENT_DAYS}
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 5.0))

    a.plot(lim, lim, color=MUTED, ls="--", lw=1, label="no difference")
    a.scatter(off, on, s=14, color=SPX_MODEL, label="one history's first halt")
    a.axvline(-100 * rules["levels"][0], color=GRID, lw=1)
    a.axhline(-100 * rules["levels"][0], color=GRID, lw=1)
    a.set_xlim(lim)

    a.set_xlabel("day's change without breakers (%)")

    a.set_title("a. The day a breaker first fires")
    a.legend(loc="upper left")
    b = ax[1]
    for i, k in enumerate(policy.EVENT_DAYS):
        m, lo, hi = (100 * x for x in diffs[k])
        b.errorbar(i, m, yerr=[[m - lo], [hi - m]], fmt="o", ms=8, color=SPX_MODEL, capsize=5, lw=1.6)

    b.axhline(0, color=MUTED, ls="--", lw=1)
    b.set_xticks(range(len(policy.EVENT_DAYS)),

    b.set_title("b. Change since the previous close (mean, 95% interval)")
    c = ax[2]

              label="same history, no surprise (placebo)")
    c.scatter(z, surprise["peak"], s=12, color=SPX_MODEL, label="with a 10% surprise")
    edges = np.array([0, 5, 10, 20, 100])
    mids, med, med0 = [], [], []
    for lo, hi in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]):

            med0.append(np.median(surprise["placebo_peak"][m] + 1))
    c.plot(mids, med, "o-", color=INK, lw=2, label="median, with the surprise")
    c.plot(mids, med0, "o--", color=SECOND, lw=1.6, label="median, placebo")
    c.axhline(1, color=MUTED, ls="--", lw=1)
    c.set_xlabel("chartists the day before the surprise (% of traders)")
    c.set_ylabel("largest fall within 10 days, in units of the surprise")
    c.set_title("c. A policy surprise: the value drops 10% at once")
    c.legend(loc="upper right")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.08, 1, 0.93))
    plots.save(fig, path, "Fig 11. Policy experiments (extension): circuit breakers and a policy surprise",
               f"S&P-calibrated model. Breakers: the US rules (15-minute pauses at -7% and -13% before 3:25 pm, "
               f"closed at -20%), "
               f"scaled x{scale:.2f} to the model's volatility; {len(breaker_seeds)} paired histories of {days:,} days "
               f"with and without breakers, compared at each history's first halt (identical until then). "
               f"Surprise: {len(surprise_seeds)} histories, one 10% drop in the value on a random day; "
               "1 = the price fell exactly as much as the value; the placebo is the same measure without the "
               "surprise (ordinary wobble); the gap between the two medians shows the overshoot roughly "
               "(paired numbers in figures/RESULTS.md).")

    for lo, hi in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]):

return k / np.sum(np.log(a[:k] / a[k]))


def kurtosis(r):
    """Excess kurtosis: 0 for a bell curve, > 0 for fat tails."""
    return np.mean(_standardize(r) ** 4) - 3


def ccdf(r):
    """Sorted |standardized returns| x and the fraction of days with |z| >= x."""
    z = np.sort(np.abs(_standardize(r)))
    return z, 1 - np.arange(len(z)) / len(z)


def acf(r, lags):
    """Autocorrelation of r at each lag (Pearson correlation of r_t and r_t+lag)."""
    z = _standardize(r)
    lags = np.atleast_1d(lags)
    if lags.size == 0 or not np.all(lags == np.round(lags)):
        raise ValueError(f"lags must be whole numbers, got {lags}")
    lags = lags.astype(int)
    if np.any(lags < 1) or np.any(lags >= len(z) - 1):
        raise ValueError(f"lags must be between 1 and {len(z) - 2}")
    return np.array([np.corrcoef(z[:-k], z[k:])[0, 1] for k in lags])


def aggregate(r, tau):
    """Returns over tau days: sums of tau consecutive daily log returns
    (a leftover partial block at the end is dropped)."""
    r = _returns(r)
    if int(tau) != tau or tau < 1 or tau > len(r):
        raise ValueError(f"tau must be a whole number from 1 to {len(r)}, got {tau}")
    tau = int(tau)
    n = len(r) // tau
    return r[:n * tau].reshape(n, tau).sum(axis=1)


def alpha_regression(r, top=0.30):
    """Tail exponent the way Lux & Marchesi (1999, Fig 2) measure it: the slope of
    log(share of days with a bigger move) against log(move size), fitted over the
    largest `top` share of days. Unlike hill_alpha, this window also covers the
    bell-shaped middle of the distribution, so the two estimates differ."""
    if not 0 < top < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"top must be between 0 and 1, got {top}")
    z, cc = ccdf(r)
    k = int(len(z) * (1 - top))
    z, cc = z[k:], cc[k:]
    keep = z > 0
    if keep.sum() < 10 or np.ptp(np.log(z[keep])) == 0:
        raise ValueError("need at least 10 distinct nonzero moves in the fitted window")
    return float(-np.polyfit(np.log(z[keep]), np.log(cc[keep]), 1)[0])


def dfa(x, scales=(16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048)):
    """Detrended fluctuation analysis (Peng et al. 1994), as in Lux & Marchesi (1999,
    Fig 3): integrate x, cut it into windows of n days, remove a straight-line trend
    in each, and measure the leftover spread F(n). Returns (scales, F)."""
    x = _returns(x)
    scales = np.asarray(scales, dtype=int)
    if np.any(scales < 4) or np.any(scales > len(x) // 4):
        raise ValueError(f"scales must be between 4 and {len(x) // 4} (a quarter of the data)")
    y = np.cumsum(x - x.mean())
    F = []
    for n in scales:
        seg = y[:len(y) // n * n].reshape(-1, n)
        t = np.arange(n)
        slope, icept = np.polyfit(t, seg.T, 1)
        F.append(np.sqrt(np.mean((seg - (np.outer(slope, t) + icept[:, None])) ** 2)))
    return scales, np.array(F)

    reversals. Lux & Marchesi (1999): returns 0.48, absolute returns 0.85."""
    s, F = dfa(x, scales)
    return float(np.polyfit(np.log(s), np.log(F), 1)[0])

# Lux & Marchesi (1999) figure conventions

Source: `paper/LuxMarchesi1999_Nature.pdf` (Nature 397:498-500), read 6 Nov 2026 from the text
and from page images rendered at 220 dpi. Written in my own words. The only quote is in Fig 2.

The paper has **three figures**, and all three show **one simulated run only**. No figure
shows real market data. The comparison with real markets is made in words, by citing other
studies: refs 17-18 for the tail exponent at daily frequency, and refs 6 and 20 for H of
absolute returns. Every "simulated next to the S&P 500" panel in this project goes beyond
the paper.

## Fig 1: a "snapshot" of a longer run (p. 498)
- **Three panels stacked vertically, sharing a linear time axis** from 0 to 4,000, labelled
  "Time" (one unit = one trading day).
- **a. "Price and fundamental value".** Linear y axis, about 100-180, labelled p, p_f.
  - The price p is a solid line; the value p_f is a dotted line.
  - The value is **shifted vertically** so the two lines can be told apart (the caption
    says so). The two lines move almost together.
- **b. "The 'output': relative price changes".** Returns ret_t = ln p_t - ln p_(t-1), drawn
  as a thin line. Linear y axis from -0.04 to +0.04.

## Fig 1 — The price follows its value, but returns are wilder than the news (paper's Fig 1)
`fig1_snapshot.png`. 4,000 days of one held-out history per setting.
- The price (a) tracks its fundamental value closely, as in the paper.
- The news (c) has kurtosis 0.0: a plain bell curve. The returns (b) have bursts
  (kurtosis 2.9 in this stretch), and the bursts line up with a high share of
  chartists (d).
- The S&P-calibrated model keeps few chartists most of the time (d, right), so
  this stretch is calm; its bursts are rarer and are shown in Fig 5.

## Fig 2 — Fat tails over a day, a bell curve over weeks (paper's Fig 2)
`fig2_tails.png`.
- **Paper-matched:** tail α (the paper's log-log fit to the largest 30% of moves)
  is **2.62 on average over 8 held-out runs of 100,000 days** (paper: 2.64 ± 0.08).
  The run shown gives 2.84. Kurtosis falls from 68 at 1 day to 1.8 at 25 days:
  the paper's **cross-over to the bell curve**.
- **S&P-calibrated:** the median kurtosis falls from 5.5 (1 day) to 1.6 (25 days).
- **Real S&P 500:** kurtosis 25 at 1 day, but still **3.3 at 25 days**. The real
  market keeps fat tails at long horizons more than either model does (1987
  matters a lot here).
- The news collapses onto the bell curve at every horizon, as in the paper.

## Fig 3 — No memory of direction, long memory of size (paper's Fig 3)
`fig3_memory.png`. Detrended fluctuation analysis (Peng et al. 1994).

| | Paper | Paper-matched (mean of 8 held-out runs) | S&P 500 | S&P-calibrated (median of the 40 Fig 7 histories) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H of returns | 0.48 | 0.47 | 0.50 | **0.39** |
| H of \|returns\| | 0.85 | 0.81 | 0.90 | 0.87 |
| H of news / \|news\| | 0.49 / 0.51 | 0.50 / 0.49 | — | — |

The figure itself shows **one run of each**, so its printed values differ a little
from these averages: paper-matched H 0.45, H|r| 0.78, news 0.47 (seed 1000);
S&P-calibrated H 0.38, H|r| 0.92 (one history). One run varies; the table is the
better summary.

The long memory in move sizes is created by the traders: the news has none.
The paper-matched H of |returns| (0.81 ± 0.02 between runs) is below the paper's 0.85 ± 0.01: not reproduced, though still far above the news's 0.49.
The S&P-calibrated model's returns **reverse** a little from day to day
(H 0.39), while the S&P's do not (0.50). This is its clearest miss (Fig 7).

## Fig 4 — The proposal's checks
## Fig 9 — How robust is it? (paper: "an open set of parameter values")
`fig9_robustness.png`. 400 random settings, one 20,000-day run each.
- **44%** run away into an endless bubble.
- Of the 222 that stay stable: **65%** give fat tails *and* long memory, 4% fat
  tails only, 32% thin tails.
- The paper is right that good settings form a whole region, not a single point.
  But the region is not "almost everything": stability is the main limit.

  The run shown gives 2.84. Kurtosis falls from 68 at 1 day to 1.8 at 25 days:
  the paper's **cross-over to the bell curve**.
- **S&P-calibrated:** the median kurtosis falls from 5.5 (1 day) to 1.6 (25 days).
- **Real S&P 500:** kurtosis 25 at 1 day, but still **3.3 at 25 days**. The real
  market keeps fat tails at long horizons more than either model does (1987
  matters a lot here).
- The news collapses onto the bell curve at every horizon, as in the paper.

## Fig 3 — No memory of direction, long memory of size (paper's Fig 3)
`fig3_memory.png`. Detrended fluctuation analysis (Peng et al. 1994).

| | Paper | Paper-matched (mean of 8 held-out runs) | S&P 500 | S&P-calibrated (median of the 40 Fig 7 histories) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H of returns | 0.48 | 0.47 | 0.50 | **0.39** |
| H of \|returns\| | 0.85 | 0.81 | 0.90 | 0.87 |
| H of news / \|news\| | 0.49 / 0.51 | 0.50 / 0.49 | — | — |

The figure itself shows **one run of each**, so its printed values differ a little
from these averages: paper-matched H 0.45, H|r| 0.78, news 0.47 (seed 1000);
S&P-calibrated H 0.38, H|r| 0.92 (one history). One run varies; the table is the
better summary.

The long memory in move sizes is created by the traders: the news has none.
The paper-matched H of |returns| (0.81 ± 0.02 between runs) is below the paper's 0.85 ± 0.01: not reproduced, though still far above the news's 0.49.
The S&P-calibrated model's returns **reverse** a little from day to day
(H 0.39), while the S&P's do not (0.50). This is its clearest miss (Fig 7).

## Fig 9 — How robust is it? (paper: "an open set of parameter values")
`fig9_robustness.png`. 400 random settings, one 20,000-day run each.
- **44%** run away into an endless bubble.
- Of the 222 that stay stable: **65%** give fat tails *and* long memory, 4% fat
  tails only, 32% thin tails.
- The paper is right that good settings form a whole region, not a single point.
  But the region is not "almost everything": stability is the main limit.

    """The straight line behind alpha_regression: (alpha, c, x_min, x_max), where the
    share of days with a bigger move is about c * x**-alpha for x_min <= x <= x_max
    (moves in standard deviations; the window is the largest `top` share of days)."""

        raise ValueError(f"top must be between 0 and 1, got {top}")
    z, cc = ccdf(r)
    k = int(len(z) * (1 - top))
    z, cc = z[k:], cc[k:]
    keep = z > 0
    if keep.sum() < 10 or np.ptp(np.log(z[keep])) == 0:
        raise ValueError("need at least 10 distinct nonzero moves in the fitted window")
    slope, icept = np.polyfit(np.log(z[keep]), np.log(cc[keep]), 1)
    return float(-slope), float(np.exp(icept)), float(z[keep][0]), float(z[-1])


def alpha_regression(r, top=0.30):
    """Tail exponent the way Lux & Marchesi (1999, Fig 2) measure it: the slope of
    log(share of days with a bigger move) against log(move size), fitted over the
    largest `top` share of days. Unlike hill_alpha, this window also covers the
    bell-shaped middle of the distribution, so the two estimates differ."""
    return tail_fit(r, top)[0]

from pathlib import Path
p = Path("herding/plots.py"); s = p.read_text()
old = s[s.index("def ccdf(ax, r, label, color, **kw):"):s.index("def standardized(r):")]
new = '''def ccdf(ax, r, label, color, points=None, **kw):
    """Log-log tail plot: share of days whose |standardized return| exceeds x.
    With `points`, draw about that many markers, spaced evenly on the log x axis and
    each on a real data point (the largest move always included), as in Lux &
    Marchesi's Fig 2; otherwise draw every point as a line."""
    z, cc = stats.ccdf(r)
    keep = z > 0
    z, cc = z[keep], cc[keep]
    if points:
        grid = np.geomspace(z[0], z[-1], points)
        i = np.unique(np.append(np.minimum(np.searchsorted(z, grid), len(z) - 1), len(z) - 1))
        z, cc = z[i], cc[i]
        kw = dict(dict(ls="none", marker="o", ms=4), **kw)
    ax.loglog(z, cc, color=color, label=label, **kw)


def gaussian_ccdf(ax, label="bell curve N(0,1)", ls="--"):
    g = np.geomspace(0.05, 6, 200)
    # share of a bell curve beyond +-x: erfc(x / sqrt 2). (math.erfc, not scipy: scipy
    # takes about half a second to load, in every worker process)
    ax.loglog(g, [erfc(x / np.sqrt(2)) for x in g], ls, color=MUTED, lw=1.2, label=label)


def power_law(ax, x0, y0, slope, x1, label=None, color=MUTED, **kw):
    """Reference line y = y0 (x / x0)^slope from x0 to x1: a straight line of the given
    slope on log-log axes (a tail exponent is minus the slope; H is the slope)."""
    x = np.array([x0, x1])
    ax.loglog(x, y0 * (x / x0) ** slope, color=color, label=label, **dict(dict(ls="--", lw=1.1), **kw))


def dfa(ax, x, scales, label, color, marker="o", shift=1.0, fit_ls="-"):
    """DFA fluctuation F(n) vs window n (log-log), with the fitted slope H in the label.
    Returns (H, the first window, its fitted F) so a reference slope can start there."""
    s, F = stats.dfa(x, scales)
    coef = np.polyfit(np.log(s), np.log(F), 1)
    ax.loglog(s, F * shift, marker, color=color, ms=4.5, lw=0, label=f"{label}: H = {coef[0]:.2f}")
    fit = np.exp(np.polyval(coef, np.log(s))) * shift
    ax.loglog(s, fit, fit_ls, color=color, lw=1.0)
    return coef[0], s[0], fit[0]


'''
